EPSG:27700 is the valid projected CRS OSGB36 / British National Grid. | Its coordinate system is Cartesian 2D with easting and northing axes measured in metres. | Its stated scope includes engineering survey and topographic mapping.
EPSG:27700 defines horizontal positioning and does not by itself specify an ODN vertical height datum. | A correct CRS identifier does not prove that a parcel polygon or elevation sample is correct.

operations.source_name: OSGB36 / British National Grid + ODN height — EPSG:7405
operations.details_summary: EPSG:7405 is the compound CRS OSGB36 / British National Grid + ODN height. | The horizontal component is EPSG:27700. | The vertical component is ODN height EPSG:5701 with a gravity-related height axis in metres.

operations.source_name: OSGB36 / British National Grid + ODN height — EPSG:7405
operations.details_summary: Compound CRS identification prevents horizontal and vertical reference conflation but does not alter raster values. | The parcel result still requires exact polygon binding, source-byte hashing and valid-pixel sampling.

operations.source_name: ETRS89 to OSGB36 / British National Grid (3) — EPSG:7953
operations.details_summary: EPSG:7953 is the OSTN15-based ETRS89-to-OSGB36 British National Grid transformation. | It is identified as the official definition of OSGB36 from August 2016. | The registry distinguishes exactness by definition from comparison accuracy against archived triangulation coordinates.

operations.source_name: ETRS89 to OSGB36 / British National Grid (3) — EPSG:7953
operations.details_summary: Exactness by definition is a reference-frame statement and is not parcel-elevation measurement accuracy. | Transformation accuracy must remain separate from LiDAR vertical RMSE and polygon uncertainty.

operations.details_summary: Conversion between latitude/longitude and eastings/northings on the same datum is a map projection operation. | That operation is not a datum transformation. | GNSS/ETRS89 to OSGB36 National Grid conversion requires OSTN15 or an explicitly lower-accuracy approximation.
